verdict.rationale: GitLab documents a broad REST API covering workflows, CI/CD across projects, and user access control. It publishes an autogenerated OpenAPI 3.0 spec with interactive testing of every endpoint and semantic versioning, but nothing in the evidence states that the API matches everything the UI can do. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement, documentation of coverage gaps or UI-only features, and independent hands-on corroboration that UI actions can all be done via the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Automate your workflows and build integrations with the GitLab REST API
Manage CI/CD processes across multiple projects with precision.
Control user access programmatically to maintain consistent permissions across your organization.
You can browse and test every endpoint interactively in the [REST API documentation]
The OpenAPI spec is autogenerated directly from the API code and is tightly coupled to its implementation, ensuring the documentation is always accurate and up to date
GitLab will not make these changes within REST API v4, and follows semantic versioning for the REST API
